name: Loomwork
tagline: Calm nonograms that weave into cloth.
description: Nonograms the way they should feel: calm, fair and beautiful. Fill the grid from the number clues to reveal a hidden picture, and every finished picture weaves into a full-colour textile for your Loom gallery. Each puzzle has exactly one solution, and a solver checks that it can be reached by line logic alone, so you never have to guess. No ads, no lives, no nags.
highlights: Over 250 original pixel pictures in 16 packs, from 5×5 up to 40×40 showpieces
Colour packs where each clue is coloured like its run, plus endless generated textiles up to 50×50
Hints that explain the next deduction in plain words, a daily puzzle with streaks, widgets, and iCloud sync
imageAlt: Loomwork: a wall of pixel-art pictures around the app name

A finished picture weaving into cloth
The Loom gallery of finished weaving

name: Out of Sorts
tagline: A word roguelike set in an old print shop.
description: A word game with a roguelike heart, set in an old letterpress shop. Set words from wood type, print them for Points × Ink, and hit each page's quota before your prints run out. Between pages, the Stationer sells dingbats, the ornaments of the printing trade, which bend the scoring rules. Eight chapters print the book, and every third page is a deadline with a twist.
highlights: 34 dingbats that fire left to right, so the order you shelve them in matters
Deadlines like the Censor, who bans a letter, and Catchwords, where each word starts with the last letter of the one before
A Daily Edition for everyone, five paper stocks to unlock, and a Specimen Book of every word you print
imageAlt: Out of Sorts: the title spelled in wood-type tiles on a dark background

gallery.alt: Printing a word for Points times Ink

name: Yuzu Springs
tagline: A cozy hot spring full of capybaras.
description: A cozy idle game set in a mountain hot spring where capybaras come to unwind. Splash the springs to earn coins, build and upgrade baths, and hire attendants who keep the steam rising while you're away. All of the art and music is procedural: the whole game is drawn and scored in code, and fits in about 200 KB.
highlights: 15 hot-spring stations, from a humble foot bath to the Moonlight Pool and the sky-high Celestial Gate
19 guests to befriend, including otters, frogs, a kitsune and a red panda
A weekly Lantern Festival with its own Night Market, and seasons that grow the resort forever
imageAlt: Yuzu Springs: capybaras and friends soaking in a mountain hot-spring resort

gallery.alt: The springs at night during the Lantern Festival

name: Brightwork
tagline: A gentle nudge when it's been a while.
description: Some things don't need a to-do list, just a nudge when it's been a while. Brightwork keeps the quiet, recurring things in your life as copper plates on a shelf: watering the plants, calling home, changing the sheets. Each plate slowly dulls as its rhythm runs out, and once you've done the thing, a press and hold makes it shine again. No ads, no account, no subscription.
highlights: A ledger for every plate, with your real pace and how often you kept it bright
One gentle nudge, at the time you choose, when something comes due
Copper, brass, bronze and silver finishes that each age their own way, verdigris included
imageAlt: Brightwork: the app icon, a copper plate with a sprout, beside the app name

gallery.alt: A plate's ledger with your real pace
Picking the first plates for your shelf

name: Longthink
tagline: A turn timer for game night.
description: Lay your phone flat in the middle of the table. Everyone gets a slice of the screen facing their seat, a brass dial turns to whoever's up, and a tap anywhere passes the turn. At the end of the night, Longthink tells you who really took their time. No account and no server: every game stays on the phone.
highlights: Stopwatch and turn timer, plus a chess clock with a time bank for each player or team
An end-of-night Reckoning with a turn-by-turn strip, honours like The Deliberator, and a shareable results card
Built for the table: 2 to 8 seats, snake and reverse turn order, teams, undo, and an auto-pause when you leave the app
imageAlt: Longthink: the app icon, a brass dial over four coloured seats, beside the app name

name: Kinma
tagline: A pet that eats what you eat.
description: A tamagotchi you feed with photos of your real meals, and that grows more sociable when you actually eat with friends. Snap a meal and Claude vision identifies the dish and cuisine; start a table and friends join with a QR code. The pet never dies and food is never scored healthy or unhealthy. It just rewards variety and company.
highlights: Two growth axes: solo meals build Nourishment, shared tables build Sociability
Pet evolution, a Closet of accessories, and a two-shade LCD retro art mode
Deferred deep links, push reminders in the pet's voice, and shared table journals
imageAlt: Kinma: three round pastel pets on a teal background

gallery.alt: Starting a shared table with a QR code

name: Capsule Cove
description: You've inherited Hoshi's Capsule Nook, a tiny figure shop in a seaside town. Pull capsules, chase every colour variant, and fill your display cases so visitors drop tips in the jar. Every figure is generated procedurally, and there is no framework or engine underneath, just canvas and ES modules.
highlights: Procedural chibi figure generator with auto-shading, outlines, and holo effects
77 figures in 11 series across a seaside town, Whisper Woods, an island, a Cloud Garden, and a glowing grotto
Fishing, digging, a claw machine, shop decorating, and a generative WebAudio lullaby
imageAlt: Capsule Cove: a pixel-art town with the Capsule Nook shop and cherry trees

gallery.alt: A decorated shop full of figure display cases

name: CatDex
tagline: Identify and collect every cat breed.
description: A Pokédex for cats. Snap any cat and AI shows the breeds it most resembles, with honest results for mixed-breed moggies. Every breed you find joins your collection with your own photo; the rest stay as silhouettes until you spot one in the wild.
highlights: Claude vision returns the top three breeds with confidence and the features that gave it away
Rarity tiers, badges, a photo journal with nicknames, and a daily breed quiz with streaks
The full breed catalogue ships inside the app, so browsing works offline
imageAlt: CatDex: a glowing red cat outline beside the app name

name: Buzzword vs. Share Price
description: An interactive narrative visualization exploring how tech buzzwords correlate with company stock price performance, told across multiple scenes.

description: An e-commerce storefront for browsing and buying plants, with a product catalog and shopping cart.
